title: Genitive Absolute (Γενικὴ Ἀπόλυτος)
description: Applies when a noun and participle stand in the Genitive case to state background circumstances. Used when the participle's subject does not appear in the main clause.
negation: μή (for hypothetical/conditional clauses) or οὐ (for factual clauses)

examples.text: τοῦ Σωκράτους λέγοντος, οἱ μαθηταὶ ἤκουον.
examples.translation: While Socrates was speaking, the disciples were listening.
When Cyrus was reigning, many good things happened.

title: Three-Case Preposition: παρά
description: Meaning shifts depending on whether it governs Genitive (source), Dative (location), or Accusative (motion/comparison).

meanings.sense: + Accusative (to the side of / along / contrary to)
